title: Weight in the first weeks
text: It's normal for babies to lose some weight in the first few days. Your baby will be weighed in their first 2 weeks, and most are back to their birth weight by 3 weeks.

title: The cord stump
text: It takes about a week to dry out and drop off. Keep it clean and dry until it does, and tell your midwife, health visitor or GP if you notice any bleeding or discharge.

title: Vitamin D from birth
text: Breastfed babies need a daily vitamin D supplement from birth. Babies having more than 500ml of formula a day don't, because formula already contains it.

title: Help with feeding
text: Your midwife and health visitor can help between appointments: their numbers are in your baby's red book. The National Breastfeeding Helpline is on 0300 100 0212, open 24 hours a day.

title: Register the birth
text: In England and Wales a birth must be registered within 42 days. Book an appointment with your local register office.

title: A high temperature under 3 months
text: A temperature of 38°C or higher in a baby under 3 months needs urgent help: call 999 or go to A&E.

title: How are you?
text: Feeling low or tearful in the first days is common and usually passes within 2 weeks of the birth. If it carries on, gets worse or you're struggling to cope, tell your midwife, health visitor or GP: they support parents too.

title: Crying
text: Babies start to cry more from about 2 weeks. It's usually at its worst at about 6 to 8 weeks, often in the afternoon and evening, then eases. It's normal and it will stop. If it gets too much, put your baby down somewhere safe and take a few minutes. Never shake a baby.

title: Your own 6-week check
text: Your GP surgery should offer you a check 6 to 8 weeks after the birth, about your own health and recovery. It's often just before or after your baby's 6 to 8 week check.

title: Getting ready for solid food
text: The NHS advises starting at around 6 months. Look for all three signs together: sitting up holding their head steady, picking food up and bringing it to their mouth, and swallowing it rather than pushing it back out.

title: Starting solid food
text: Around now is the time to start, once your baby shows all three signs. Offer a cup of water with meals from now too.

title: Vitamins from 6 months
text: The government recommends a daily supplement of vitamins A, C and D from 6 months to 5 years, unless your baby has more than 500ml of formula a day.

title: Sleeping in your room
text: The Lullaby Trust advises having your baby sleep in the same room as you, day and night, for at least the first 6 months.

title: First teeth
text: Most babies start teething at around 6 months, though some start before 4 months and some after their first birthday. Start brushing twice a day, with a smear of fluoride toothpaste, as soon as the first tooth comes through.

title: Keep out of strong sun
text: Babies under 6 months should be kept out of direct strong sunlight.

title: Milk and bottles at 1
text: From 12 months, whole cows' milk can be their main drink, and the NHS advises moving away from bottles once they're 1. An open or free-flow cup is better for their teeth.
